expectations.text: Applies the two-step test: Annex I (high criticality) vs Annex II sectors, then size thresholds (generally 250+/€50M for essential in Annex I; medium-size entities typically important)
expectations.evidence: Annex I vs. Annex II sector step, then size: 'Essential Entity if you're in an Annex I sector AND... ≥250 employees, OR turnover >€50M'; worked example defaults medium Annex I entity to Important

expectations.text: States the supervision difference: essential = ex-ante AND ex-post (inspections, audits); important = ex-post only, triggered by evidence
expectations.evidence: Essential: 'Ex-ante *and* ex-post: proactive on-site inspections, regular... audits'; Important: 'Ex-post only: triggered by evidence or indication of non-compliance'

expectations.text: States the fine floors: ≥€10M or 2% worldwide turnover (essential) vs ≥€7M or 1.4% (important)
expectations.evidence: Higher of €10,000,000 or 2% of total worldwide annual turnover [essential] vs Higher of €7,000,000 or 1.4% [important]

expectations.text: Mentions management liability including potential temporary bans from managerial functions (essential entities)
expectations.evidence: Personal liability, with possible temporary ban from managerial functions [essential]

expectations.text: Notes special designations: CER-designated critical entities are automatically essential regardless of size; some sectors (e.g., qualified trust/DNS/TLD) essential regardless of size
expectations.evidence: an entity designated critical under the CER Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (CER designation flows automatically into essential-entity status)... qualified trust service provider, TLD registry, DNS provider... automatically essential regardless of size
